sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Sachin Parmar, learned counsel for the appellants.
Shri Rajesh Pandit, learned counsel for the respondent
ORDER 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 20.06.2023 passed in MACC No.168/2021 by the Additional Member to the First Member Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur,
District Dhar whereby a total sum of Rs.8,47,600/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur,
District Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. As per the appellants, on 02.01.2021 at about 5.30 p.m. the deceased Ashok along with his wife Anita was going from Indore to Amjhera for a function on a motor cycle.

Near Rajpura Waiting Hall a car bearing registration No.MP-09- CX-4032 owned by respondent No.2 and being driven by respondent No.1 and which was insured with respondent No.3 came from the opposite side.
The same was being driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.1.
The car dashed against the motorcycle of Ashok as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment but eventually expired.

3. The appellants therefore filed an application under Section 166 of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:35354 2 MA-5597-2024 Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of compensation in the sum of Rs.40,00,000/- to them on account of death of Ashok.
The claim petition was resisted by respondent No.3 by filing reply to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded the compensation as aforesaid.

1 4.
This appeal has been preferred on the ground that the income of the deceased has been assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month which is inordinately low.
Even if the deceased had been considered to be unemployed then also looking to his age his income ought to have been assessed appropriately.
The guidelines as have been issued by the NALSA and also by the Collector from time to time and which were in force on the date of the accident ought to have been taken into consideration.
In not doing so the Claims Tribunal has committed an illegality.

5. Per contra learned counsel for respondent No.3 has submitted that on the basis of the evidence brought on record the income of the deceased has been correctly fixed by the Claims Tribunal in which there is no reason to interfere in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
7. The accident in question took place on 02.01.2021.

Even if the deceased was to be considered as unemployed then also his income ought to have been assessed in view of the guidelines issued by NALSA in that regard and also by taking into consideration the minimum wages as fixed by the Government itself.
The income which has been assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month does appear to be inordinately low.
Taking the assistance of the aforesaid guidelines the income of the deceased ought to have been assessed at Rs.8,400/- per month.

In not doing NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:35354 3 MA-5597-2024 so the Claims Tribunal has acted erroneously.

8. The amount to be awarded to the appellants by way of loss of dependency would hence work out at Rs.8,400/- per month being the income of the deceased and adding 10% future prospects of Rs.840/- to the same looking to the age of the deceased it would come to Rs.9,240/-.

Multiplying the same by 12 for assessing the yearly income and deducting one third therefrom and applying the multiplier of 11 looking to the age of the deceased which was 51 years the total amount for loss of dependency would come to Rs.8,13,120/-.
The other amounts which have been awarded by the Claims Tribunal for medical expenses, loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses are just and proper.
9. Thus the total amount which the appellants deserve to be awarded is Rs.9,83,120/- whereas the Claims Tribunal has awarded them a sum of Rs.8,47,600/- only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for award of additional compensation in the sum of Rs.1,35,520/- which shall be payable to them by respondent No.3 along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
Appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE ns Anitabai vs Sureshchandra on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193089465/
